 Tsitsipas is the deserved favourite and most likely books his spot in the semi-finals. 
 The Greek has been in resurgent form over the last couple of months, going 19-7 since July and registering a 11-1 record vs 50+ ranked players during that period. 
 Duckworth meanwhile is into the Almaty Open quarter-finals for the second straight year. The Aussie veteran thrives in Almaty and is coming off a straight sets victory over Luciano Darderi, where he served 17 aces. Ducks also conquered Flavio Cobolli at this tournament last year. 
 I can't see Duckworth pulling off the upset here - after all, he's 4-10 in ATP quarter-finals and only has 17 top 40 victories since 2012. 
 But if he maintains that level of serving, Duckworth can push this match Over 20.5 total games and perhaps even snatch a set.

 Tsitsipas has struggled considerably over the last few years, but he's slowly getting back to a high level and he's actually inside the top 15 this year in terms of total match wins. 
If he maintains this sort of form for the remainder of 2026, he should be able to get into the seeding positions for the 2027 Australian Open. 
 The Greek comes into this clash having won 19 of his last 26 matches, including claiming the title in Gstaad and making the R16 of the US Open and Shanghai Masters. 
 Tsitsipas survived Aleksandar Kovacevic in three sets in his Almaty opener before ending the career of Kazakh veteran Mikhail Kukushkin to make the quarter-finals, easing to a 6-1 6-2 victory. James Duckworth Form Analysis
 2026 ATP Record: 14-20
 ATP Almaty Record: 5-2
 Current Ranking: No. 73
 Career-High Ranking: No. 46 (2022)
 Duckworth is the classic Aussie battler, fighting back from countless surgeries to reclaim a spot inside the top 100 this year - and he'll be determined to keep push back towards the top 50. 
 The 34-year-old is underrated indoors - he made the Paris Masters quarter-finals back in 2021, while he's won five of his seven matches in Almaty, backing up his run to the semi-finals last year by returning to the last eight here. 
 Duckworth took a set off Daniil Medvedev before falling in the final four last year and he's given himself a chance to make the semi-finals again after toppling Miomir Kecmanovic and Darderi in straight sets this week.
